title: U.S. Stocks Rise as AI Bets Offset Bond Yield Fears
source_used: Reuters wire text (AOL.com copy); TradingView News; Chosunbiz (Yonhap-based, AI-translated). WSJ original not opened (HTTP 401).
key_facts: Reuters: the Nasdaq closed at a record on Monday 5 Oct 2026, up 1.05% at 27,477.31, lifted by Nvidia and Microsoft; its previous record close was 22 Sep.
Reuters: the S&P 500 rose 0.66% to 7,773.95, about 0.3% below its 13 Aug record close; the Dow rose 0.18% to 51,267.90.
Reuters: Nvidia rose 2.1% to a record close, valued at $5.76 trillion; Microsoft gained 1.5%; Meta and Tesla about 2% each.

Reuters: optimism about corporate earnings has helped US stocks beat global rivals over six months despite rising Treasury yields; analysts expect S&P 500 earnings to jump over 30% year on year, largely from AI-related stocks (LSEG data).

TradingView News: the US 10-year yield closed at 5.31% and the 30-year at 5.664%, their highest settlements since 2002; higher long-term borrowing costs can affect mortgages, corporate financing and the valuation of future profits.

Chosunbiz: the 10-year yield rose intraday to 5.347%, the highest since April 2002; Jay Hatfield of Infrastructure Capital said tech stocks have served as a safe haven because strong computing demand makes them less affected by rising rates.
Reuters: weaker US jobs data on Friday cut the chance of a Fed rate hike this month to 24% from 70% a week ago (CME FedWatch); Q3 earnings season starts next week with large banks.
quote_evidence: The Nasdaq notched a record high close on Monday, lifted by Nvidia and Microsoft, as investors focused on a dip in oil prices and looked ahead to quarterly earnings reports.
Optimism about robust corporate earnings has helped US stocks outperform global rivals in the last six months, despite rising Treasury yields and higher oil prices related to the US war with Iran.
The US 10-year Treasury yield closed at 5.31% and the 30-year at 5.664%, their highest settlements since 2002.
why_it_matters_hint: Stocks held up because investors expect AI-driven profits to grow, even with long-term US borrowing costs at their highest since 2002.
